object_description: A frozen equal-budget allocation-comparison instrument (worlds/dynamics/arms/metric/budget) used to decide whether a learner-conditioned adaptive allocation policy beats a static structural parent. The object under study is the INSTRUMENT, not any allocator.
qoi: ADMISSIBLE / INADMISSIBLE / CANNOT_CHECK: can this instrument, under its own equal-budget constraint, produce an arm separation at or above its own registered minimum detectable effect for ANY state-aware allocation policy, including an omniscient one?
scope: equal-budget arm comparisons where every arm spends an identical number of training examples
instruments whose generative parameters are fully known to the experimenter (simulated / model-free development stress)
instruments that register a minimum detectable effect or a hard promotion gate on a primary arm contrast
NOT_IN_SCOPE: real-model experiments whose generative parameters are unknown and whose oracle cannot be computed (these must return CANNOT_CHECK)
assumptions: the instrument's per-example outcome dynamics are computable by the experimenter
an oracle policy with full generative-parameter access is constructible under the identical budget constraint
the registered minimum detectable effect is frozen before the ceiling is computed
the ceiling multiplier kappa is frozen before any instrument is evaluated by the gate
the oracle is a greedy or exact upper bound and is reported as which of the two it is

strongest_parents.cost_equation: cost = 0 additional simulation runs; analytic in n and variance
strongest_parents.justification: Preregistered MDE plus power analysis is the standard and strongest incumbent method for deciding whether a comparison can resolve an effect. It is the correct parent to beat because it is what the frozen Paper IV protocols already use.

implementation_refs: literature: oracle/skyline baselines in information retrieval and recommender evaluation
literature: regret-versus-oracle formulations in bandit and online-allocation analysis
literature: ceiling analysis in applied machine-learning pipeline debugging
strongest_parents.justification: Oracle/skyline baselines are established prior art for bounding achievable performance. The parent reports the oracle descriptively; it does not convert it into a pre-execution admissibility decision bound to a registered MDE.

prior_art_equivalence_map: classical power analysis == bounds sampling noise for a HYPOTHESIZED effect size; this mechanic bounds the ACHIEVABLE effect size itself and is therefore not reducible to it
oracle/skyline baseline == same computation, but reported as a descriptive upper reference rather than as a frozen pre-execution admissibility gate against a registered MDE
ceiling analysis (component-wise upper-bound substitution) == same intuition applied to pipeline components; here applied to an experimental instrument's arm-separation capacity
regret-versus-oracle == same oracle object; regret evaluates a policy, this gate evaluates the instrument

assay positive control == structurally the closest analogue: an instrument that cannot register a known-positive signal is inadmissible. This mechanic is the equal-budget allocation instance of that principle, with the positive control supplied by an omniscient policy rather than a spiked sample.
oracle_or_lower_bound: ORACLE_GREEDY_CEILING: at every example slot, select the coordinate maximizing the exact expected immediate change in the registered primary metric under the instrument's true generative rates and true harm terms, subject to the identical total budget. Reported explicitly as a GREEDY upper reference, not a proven global optimum; a proven-optimal solver upgrades the bound but never weakens it. Reference implementation: experiments/orion_closure/run_p4_allocator_attribution.py::run_arm arm ORACLE_GREEDY_CEILING.
minimal_counterexamples: DEGENERATE_ZERO_HEADROOM: an instrument in which every arm is structurally forced to the identical allocation. Oracle ceiling is exactly 0. The gate must return INADMISSIBLE for any positive registered MDE.

GENUINE_HEADROOM: an instrument whose worlds differ in INITIAL learner state so that state information is decision-relevant, with oracle ceiling well above the registered MDE. The gate must return ADMISSIBLE.
UNCOMPUTABLE_ORACLE: a real-model instrument whose generative parameters are unknown. The gate must return CANNOT_CHECK and must NOT return ADMISSIBLE.

TIGHT_CI_LOW_CEILING: an instrument with very tight bootstrap confidence intervals but an oracle ceiling below the MDE. Classical power analysis returns 'amply powered'; the gate must still return INADMISSIBLE. This is the case actually observed in research/paper4_allocator_attribution_v1/ATTRIBUTION_RECEIPT.json.

CEILING_JUST_ABOVE_MDE: oracle ceiling above the MDE but below kappa times the MDE. The gate must return INADMISSIBLE under the frozen kappa and must not be rescued by lowering kappa after the ceiling is seen.
falsifier: The gate is refuted if an instrument it classifies INADMISSIBLE nonetheless produces a replicable, distinguishable arm separation at or above its own registered minimum detectable effect under the identical equal-budget constraint by any implementable policy. It is also refuted if the greedy oracle is shown to understate the achievable ceiling by a margin that flips an INADMISSIBLE verdict on any fresh-assurance case.
same_system_ablation: Replace the omniscient oracle with the strongest implementable state-aware policy available at freeze time and recompute admissibility on every fresh-assurance case. If verdicts are unchanged across all cases, the oracle component is not carrying the mechanic and the gate reduces to ordinary strongest-parent reporting; the novelty residual would then be withdrawn.
hard_gate_obligations: fail closed: return CANNOT_CHECK, never ADMISSIBLE, when the oracle is not computable under the instrument's own generative model
kappa and the registered minimum detectable effect are frozen before the ceiling is computed and may never be revised after ceiling access
an INADMISSIBLE verdict may never be upgraded by access to arm outcomes
the gate never promotes, revives, or reverses any allocator terminal; it only decides whether a comparison is worth executing
oracle rollout cost is charged to the comparison's total cost, not hidden
the greedy-versus-exact status of the oracle bound is reported with every verdict
an ADMISSIBLE verdict grants no scientific authority and no expectation that any policy will in fact win
total_cost_equation: total_cost = oracle_rollout_cost + ceiling_bootstrap_cost, where oracle_rollout_cost = n_worlds * n_replicates * budget * per_example_replan_cost and ceiling_bootstrap_cost = bootstrap_repetitions * n_world_replicates. This cost is charged to the comparison it gates and must be reported even when the verdict is ADMISSIBLE.
novelty_residual: Classical power analysis and preregistered MDE bound SAMPLING NOISE for an assumed effect size; they are silent on whether the instrument can generate that effect at all. The observed Paper IV development-stress instrument has bootstrap confidence intervals of width approximately 0.0016 on the primary contrast - by conventional standards amply powered - while its omniscient equal-budget ceiling is +0.00148 against a frozen promotion gate of 0.05, i.e. approximately 34 times below the gate. No arrangement of sample size can repair this. The residual claimed here is the conversion of an oracle/skyline computation into a frozen pre-execution admissibility decision bound to the registered MDE, with fail-closed CANNOT_CHECK when the oracle is not computable.
permitted_publication_claim: Method-level only: an equal-budget allocation comparison is uninformative about its registered estimand when its achievable oracle ceiling lies below its registered minimum detectable effect, and this failure mode is invisible to conventional power analysis. Demonstrated on exactly one preserved Paper IV model-free instrument. This claims nothing about learner-conditioned structural allocation efficacy in real models, does not reverse the preserved adaptive-v1 negative, and does not substitute for the frozen 7B Phase-2 protocol.
